title: Revisiting Cognition in Neural Cognitive Diagnosis

problem.claim: Cognitive diagnosis aims to measure students' proficiency on knowledge concepts from practice data.

gap.claim: Existing methods simplify proficiency into a narrowly defined latent trait and do not explicitly model cognitive factors, limiting performance and interpretability.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes a cognition-aware cognitive diagnosis model that introduces cognition as a bridge alongside student, exercise, and knowledge-concept factors.
The model explicitly represents cognitive-process dimensions through Subjective Cognitive Ability and Objective Cognitive Attribute, which are combined into a cognition-aware latent trait.
The model uses a two-stage diagnostic process combining an interaction function, a slip-and-guess influence function, a new latent trait, a continuous Q-matrix, and other features.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the cognition-aware cognitive diagnosis model and its two cognition concepts as novel or innovative contributions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on real-world datasets.
The authors report superior effectiveness and good interpretability.

narrative_sequence.summary: Cognitive diagnosis measures student proficiency on knowledge concepts using practice data.
Traditional and existing methods represent proficiency with latent traits while treating cognitive factors implicitly or narrowly.
The lack of explicit cognitive-factor modeling is reported to limit performance and interpretability.
CCD introduces cognition representations and a two-stage diagnostic process using cognitive-process dimensions, cognition-aware latent traits, and interaction functions.
Experiments on real-world datasets are reported to show superior effectiveness and good interpretability.

source_observation.claim: Explicitly modeling cognitive-process dimensions can connect student and exercise representations to a cognition-aware latent trait.

interpretation.claim: Making previously implicit cognitive factors explicit may improve the explanatory structure of a diagnosis model.

application.claim: For educational diagnosis systems, represent student-side and exercise-side cognitive attributes separately before combining them into proficiency estimation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this representation improves outcomes across domains beyond the reported real-world datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not detail the continuous Q-matrix construction or the two-stage optimization procedure.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported effectiveness or interpretability.
